text:
maria: Heads-up — the Python sample notebook on the onboarding page is failing for new users. Link in the README points to a 404 and a cell import is outdated. Seen several support tickets today. :facepalm:

maria: page: https://docs.redwood.ai/python/notebooks/getting_started.ipynb (404 when clicking 'raw' -> requirements.txt)

maria: failing cell error: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client_v1'` — we changed the package path to `redwood.client` a while back.

kevin: ugh, thanks for flagging. Is the notebook in docs repo or in the sample-apps repo?

maria: sample-apps (notebooks/sample-onboarding). The README links to `raw.githubusercontent.com/redwood/sample-apps/main/notebooks/requirements.txt` which 404s after we moved the file. Also the notebook uses `from redwood.client_v1 import Client` in cell 2.

tara: I can repro locally. `pip install -r requirements.txt` step fails because file is missing, so folks copy/paste and then hit the import error. Quick fix would be to update the README link and change the import to `from redwood import Client` (that matches the current SDK).

kevin: can we just hotfix with a tiny PR? Who owns sample-apps?

sam: I own the repo — will open a PR. Plan: 1) update READMEs to point to raw link in `main` tree 2) update notebook import 3) add a CI check to run nbconvert --execute on notebooks so link rot / import errors fail fast.

maria: :+1: please also add a note in the quickstart about using the `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var and `pip install "redwood>=0.9"` (we changed the major import surface in 0.9 and some onboarding users are on 0.8).

docs-bot: CI: sample-apps/notebooks build failed (nbbuild) — check https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/3456 (logs attached)

sam: creating PR now: https://github.com/redwood/sample-apps/pull/107 — includes link fix, import change, and a simple nb-execute CI job.

kevin: thanks. Can we also add a short note in the Python quickstart page that the notebook is kept in sample-apps repo and to refer to the pinned tag if they want snapshot reproducibility? avoids future link rot.

tara: agreed. maybe add a tiny test in docs pipeline that verifies raw links referenced in READMEs return 200. Low effort but catches this early.

maria: filing a followup ticket to add the link-check and update quickstart copy: UX-3456.

sam: PR merged to fix the immediate problem, will follow up on CI/tests. cc @kevin @tara

kevin: awesome, closing the loop. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :tada:
